chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَالٍ، عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ، عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ، عَنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قُلْنَا لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: إِنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَجْلَانَ مَرِضَ مَرَضَهُ الَّذِي مَاتَ فِيهِ، وَكَانَ يَقُولُ: إِنِّي لَا أَمُوتُ مِنْ مَرَضِي هَذَا، فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: أَيَّهَاتَ أَيَّهَاتَ، إِنْ ذَهَبَ ابْنُ عَجْلَانَ لَمْ يَعْرِفْهُ اللَّهُ قَبِيحًا مِنْ عَمَلِهِ، إِنَّ مُوسَى بْنَ عِمْرَانَ اخْتَارَ قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا، فَلَمَّا أَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ كَانَ مُوسَى أَوَّلَ مَنْ قَامَ مِنْهَا، فَقَالَ: يَا رَبِّ أَصْحَابِي، قَالَ: يَا مُوسَى إِنِّي أَبْدِلُكَ مِنْهُمْ خَيْرًا، قَالَ: رَبِّ إِنِّي وَجَدْتُ رِيحَهُمْ وَعَرَفْتُ أَسْمَاءَهُمْ – قَالَ ذَلِكَ ثَلَاثًا – فَبَعَثَهُمُ اللَّهُ أَنْبِيَاءَ

translations.en: We said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Verily, 'Abdullah ibn 'Ajlan fell sick with the sickness due to which he died, and he used to say: I am not going to die from this sickness of mine.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'How far! How far! If Ibn 'Ajlan has gone, may Allah not acquaint him with any evil arising out of his actions. Verily, Musa ibn 'Imran chose seventy men from among his people, so when the earthquake overtook them, Musa was the first to stand up after it, he said: O my Lord, my companions! He said: O Musa, I will substitute them with better than them for you. He said: O my Lord, I have gotten used to their scent and familiarized myself with their names' – he said this three times – 'so Allah resurrected them as prophets.'

en.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi highlights the theological principle of divine knowledge overriding human presumption, as Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects 'Abdullah ibn 'Ajlan's confidence in survival by linking it to the quality of his deeds. The parallel with the seventy men of Musa (AS) serves to illustrate that while intercession is possible, the ultimate destiny is determined by Allah's will, with the seventy being elevated to prophethood as a reward for their selection. This underscores the Shia emphasis on the Imam's insight into the spiritual states of individuals and the transformative power of divine grace.
en.seo_question: What is the story of Musa and the seventy men mentioned in Rijal al-Kashshi?

key_terms.ابن عجلان: Ibn 'Ajlan (a companion known for his specific illness and death)
